questions.promptHtml: A team needs a low-latency classifier that runs economically at high request volume and does not require broad world knowledge. Which model category should it evaluate first?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Small language models can provide lower latency and cost for bounded tasks when their quality is sufficient.

Reference: Foundry model concepts
questions.extraHtml: Use task fit rather than model size as the decision rule. Large reasoning models favor complex reasoning; multimodal generation is appropriate when image or audio generation is required. Benchmark quality, latency, and cost on representative data.

questions.promptHtml: An app must answer questions about photographs and accompanying text in one request. Which model type best meets the requirement?
questions.rationaleHtml:
A multimodal model can jointly process visual and textual inputs for grounded responses.

Reference: Foundry model concepts
questions.extraHtml: Embedding models encode similarity but do not independently reason over images. Speech synthesis produces audio. Multimodal models are selected when the task crosses input modalities such as text and vision.

questions.promptHtml: A company wants grounded chat over policies with keyword matching, semantic similarity, filters, and managed indexing. Which service is the best fit?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Azure AI Search provides managed indexing plus keyword, vector, hybrid, and semantic search capabilities.

Reference: Azure AI Search overview
questions.extraHtml: Blob Storage is a content source, not a relevance engine. Cosmos DB can support vector workloads but does not provide the same integrated enrichment and semantic ranking toolchain. Search is the purpose-built grounding service.

questions.promptHtml: A RAG workload must preserve exact product-code matches while also finding semantically similar passages. Which retrieval method should be selected?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Hybrid search combines full-text and vector queries so exact tokens and semantic similarity both contribute.

Reference: Hybrid search overview
questions.extraHtml: Keyword search protects exact identifiers; vector search captures conceptual similarity. Hybrid retrieval fuses both result sets, often followed by semantic ranking. It is preferable when neither lexical nor semantic evidence alone is sufficient.

questions.promptHtml: Documents change hourly and answers must reflect updates quickly. Which indexing approach best reduces staleness without rebuilding everything?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Incremental indexing processes changed source content on a frequent schedule and limits unnecessary reprocessing.

Reference: Indexers overview
questions.extraHtml: A monthly rebuild violates freshness, while an indefinite answer cache preserves stale facts. Use source change detection, indexing schedules, and freshness monitoring together; choose push ingestion when even shorter latency is required.

questions.promptHtml: An agent needs durable conversation state shared across application instances. What should the architecture use?
questions.rationaleHtml:
A persistent store keeps conversation state available across restarts and horizontally scaled instances.

Reference: Agent threads and messages
questions.extraHtml: Process memory is ephemeral and instance-bound. Model parameters are not per-user memory. Keep identity-scoped state in a durable thread or data store, apply retention controls, and avoid placing sensitive data into prompts unnecessarily.

questions.promptHtml: An agent must retrieve approved policy passages but must never update the source repository. Which integration design follows least privilege?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Read-only retrieval permissions provide the required knowledge while minimizing the agent blast radius.

Reference: Agent tools overview
questions.extraHtml: Owner access exceeds the task, and embedded credentials create secret exposure. Treat tools as security boundaries: scope identities, validate arguments, restrict operations, and log calls independently of the model response.

questions.promptHtml: A production AI application needs separate lifecycle management for prompts, evaluations, connections, and deployments. Which organizing construct should the team use?
questions.rationaleHtml:
A Foundry project organizes AI development assets, connections, evaluations, and application workflows.

Reference: Microsoft Foundry overview
questions.extraHtml: Storage containers hold objects but do not manage the AI lifecycle. VM scale sets manage compute. Projects provide a collaboration and governance boundary; use separate projects or environments where release isolation requires it.

questions.promptHtml: A model endpoint has predictable sustained demand and requires reserved throughput with stable latency. Which deployment option is most appropriate?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Provisioned deployment reserves model throughput for predictable, latency-sensitive production demand.

Reference: Azure OpenAI deployment types
questions.extraHtml: Pay-as-you-go serverless deployment favors variable demand; batch inference favors asynchronous jobs. Provisioned capacity is justified by steady utilization and throughput assurance, not merely by a high short-lived peak.

questions.promptHtml: A team evaluates several catalog models without managing hosting infrastructure and pays according to usage. Which option best fits?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Serverless API deployment exposes supported models without requiring the team to provision hosting infrastructure.

Reference: Deploy models as serverless APIs
questions.extraHtml: Managed or self-hosted compute provides more infrastructure control but adds operations. Serverless endpoints accelerate model comparison and variable workloads; verify model, region, quota, and billing availability before selection.

questions.promptHtml: A release pipeline must promote a tested prompt and agent configuration without manual portal edits. What should the team implement?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Version control plus automated deployment makes promotion repeatable, reviewable, and auditable.

Reference: CI/CD for Foundry
questions.extraHtml: Portal sessions are not reproducible, and production-only experiments bypass quality gates. Treat prompts, evaluations, infrastructure, and agent definitions as release artifacts with environment-specific configuration and rollback points.

questions.promptHtml: A CI pipeline deploys to test and production. Production uses different endpoints and identities. How should configuration be handled?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Environment-specific parameters separate deployable logic from endpoint, identity, and connection values.

Reference: CI/CD for Foundry
questions.extraHtml: Hard-coding impedes safe promotion; ad hoc copying is error-prone and unaudited. Keep secrets outside source control, use federated pipeline identity, and require the same validation gates in each environment.

questions.promptHtml: Users receive throttling errors although the endpoint is healthy. Monitoring shows requests exceed the deployment token rate. What is the most direct action?

options.label: Increase quota or reduce request rate

questions.correctLabel: Increase quota or reduce request rate
questions.rationaleHtml:
Rate-limit failures require demand shaping, quota changes, or capacity changes rather than unrelated data or safety changes.

Reference: Azure OpenAI quotas and limits
questions.extraHtml: Use bounded retries with server guidance, request queues, token budgeting, and regional capacity planning. Search corpus size and content filters do not increase the model deployment rate limit.

questions.promptHtml: A chatbot cost spike is caused by repeatedly sending an entire long conversation. Which change most directly lowers token consumption while retaining relevant context?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Context summarization and selective history reduce input tokens while preserving information needed for the next turn.

Reference: Prompt engineering concepts
questions.extraHtml: Higher output limits can increase cost, and duplicated instructions consume more tokens. Combine a context budget with retrieval and durable memory so only relevant state enters each model call.

questions.promptHtml: A team must determine whether answer quality declined after a retrieval change. Which telemetry should it compare first?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Groundedness and retrieval relevance directly reveal whether answers remain supported by useful retrieved evidence.

Reference: Foundry evaluators
questions.extraHtml: Infrastructure telemetry can explain availability but not evidence quality. Segment evaluation by corpus, query class, and release; pair offline test sets with production traces to distinguish retrieval regressions from generation regressions.

questions.promptHtml: An indexer completes successfully, but newly uploaded files never appear in search. Which operational check is most relevant?

options.label: Inspect ingestion status and source change detection

questions.correctLabel: Inspect ingestion status and source change detection
questions.rationaleHtml:
Indexer execution details and change-detection configuration identify skipped or failed source documents.

Reference: Monitor indexers
questions.extraHtml: A successful top-level run can still include document-level warnings or unsupported changes. Generation and speech settings are downstream. Monitor document counts, failures, latency, and freshness separately.

questions.promptHtml: An application running on Azure must call a model endpoint without storing keys. Which authentication method is preferred?

options.label: A shared key in the prompt

questions.rationaleHtml:
Managed identity and role-based access provide keyless authentication with centrally scoped permissions.

Reference: Azure AI services authentication
questions.extraHtml: Keys in code or prompts can leak and are difficult to scope. Assign only the data-plane role required, separate deployment management from inference, and use workload identity for supported non-Azure hosts.

questions.promptHtml: A regulated workload requires model traffic to remain on private network paths and public endpoint access to be blocked. Which design is appropriate?

options.label: Public endpoint with a complex key
Private endpoint with public access disabled

questions.correctLabel: Private endpoint with public access disabled
questions.rationaleHtml:
A private endpoint provides private addressability; disabling public access closes the public network path.

Reference: Configure private networking
questions.extraHtml: Authentication alone does not provide network isolation, and browser invocation exposes the endpoint surface. Plan private DNS and connectivity for developers, pipelines, tools, and dependent services.

questions.promptHtml: A security team must block a known list of prohibited internal project names in model inputs and outputs. Which control is most targeted?
questions.rationaleHtml:
A custom blocklist targets organization-specific terms in content filtering flows.

Reference: Use a custom blocklist
questions.extraHtml: Rate limits control volume, not content. Search profiles rank documents. Blocklists are deterministic term controls and should complement, not replace, category filters and broader data-loss prevention.

questions.promptHtml: A RAG system ingests untrusted webpages containing instructions aimed at overriding the system prompt. Which protection directly addresses this risk?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Prompt Shields can detect indirect prompt attacks embedded in third-party documents used for grounding.

Reference: Prompt Shields
questions.extraHtml: Embedding size and replica count do not classify malicious instructions. Also isolate retrieved data from trusted instructions, constrain tools, validate outputs, and avoid granting the model unnecessary authority.

questions.promptHtml: Before releasing an agent, a team needs repeatable measurements of harmful-content risk on a representative dataset. What should it run?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Safety evaluators quantify relevant content and security risks against a controlled evaluation dataset.

Reference: Risk and safety evaluators
questions.extraHtml: Network and storage tests are operational checks, not behavioral safety evidence. Establish release thresholds, retain datasets and evaluator versions, and supplement automated metrics with human review for high-impact use cases.

questions.promptHtml: Auditors must reconstruct which sources and tool calls contributed to an agent decision. Which implementation provides the strongest evidence?

options.label: A screenshot of the final answer

questions.rationaleHtml:
Traces and provenance connect a response to retrieval results, prompts, model calls, and tool activity.

Reference: Foundry observability
questions.extraHtml: Counts lack per-run causality, while screenshots omit hidden steps. Protect logs as sensitive data, apply retention and redaction, and correlate traces with deployment and prompt versions.

questions.promptHtml: An expense agent may prepare reimbursements but payments above a threshold require a person to approve execution. Which control should be implemented?

options.label: Human approval before the payment tool

questions.correctLabel: Human approval before the payment tool
questions.rationaleHtml:
A human-in-the-loop approval gate constrains high-impact tool execution while allowing lower-risk automation.

Reference: Human-in-the-loop workflows
questions.extraHtml: Temperature changes randomness, not authorization. Automatic retries can amplify harm. Place deterministic policy checks outside the model and record the approver, decision, arguments, and resulting action.

questions.promptHtml: An agent needs only calendar availability but its connector can also delete events. What is the best governance action?

options.label: Give the agent the full connector
Rely on the system prompt alone

questions.rationaleHtml:
A narrowly scoped tool schema and identity enforce least privilege beyond prompt instructions.

Reference: Agent tools overview
questions.extraHtml: Prompts are not authorization boundaries. Avoid exposing unused destructive operations, validate all tool arguments server-side, and separate read and write identities where practical.

questions.promptHtml: A deployment serves users in several regions and one region reaches quota. Which plan best improves resilience?

options.label: Route across independently provisioned regional deployments
Put all quota in the saturated region

questions.correctLabel: Route across independently provisioned regional deployments
questions.rationaleHtml:
Regional deployments with health- and capacity-aware routing reduce dependence on one regional quota pool.

Reference: Deployment options
questions.extraHtml: Concentrating quota preserves the single bottleneck. Unbounded retries worsen overload. Confirm data residency, model availability, quota, and failover behavior for every target region.

questions.promptHtml: A team wants alerts when a new prompt version increases latency and token use. Which observability design is most useful?

options.label: Trace model calls with version and token attributes
Record only monthly Azure cost totals
Sample only successful HTTP status codes

questions.correctLabel: Trace model calls with version and token attributes
questions.rationaleHtml:
Per-call traces linked to prompt versions support latency breakdowns, token analysis, and regression detection.

Reference: Foundry observability
questions.extraHtml: Monthly totals are too coarse and success-only sampling hides failures. Track retrieval, model, and tool spans; define service-level indicators and redact sensitive prompt content.

questions.promptHtml: A public-facing agent can propose actions with legal impact. Which operating mode best manages risk during initial rollout?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Semiautonomous operation adds human oversight at consequential boundaries while collecting evidence for later tuning.

Reference: Human-in-the-loop workflows
questions.extraHtml: Autonomy should be earned through measured reliability and bounded impact. Unlogged operation prevents audit and learning. Define escalation, timeout, override, and rollback behavior before expanding autonomy.

questions.promptHtml: A team must compare two model deployments while holding prompts and test cases constant. Which method yields defensible results?

options.label: Run both against the same evaluation dataset

questions.correctLabel: Run both against the same evaluation dataset
questions.rationaleHtml:
A shared representative dataset and common evaluators isolate model differences and support repeatability.

Reference: Evaluate generative AI apps
questions.extraHtml: Anecdotes and catalog text do not control inputs. Track model and evaluator versions, confidence intervals, latency, cost, safety, and task quality rather than relying on one aggregate score.

questions.promptHtml: A Python application must use project connections and deployed assets consistently across environments. What should it use?
questions.rationaleHtml:
The SDK provides supported programmatic access to project-scoped resources and connections.

Reference: Foundry SDK overview
questions.extraHtml: Portal scraping and cookies are brittle and insecure. Externalize project endpoint and deployment names, authenticate with token credentials, and use separate identities per environment.

questions.promptHtml: A support assistant must answer only from approved manuals and cite the retrieved passages. Which pattern should be implemented?
questions.rationaleHtml:
RAG retrieves approved evidence and supplies it to generation so answers can be grounded and cited.

Reference: RAG overview
questions.extraHtml: An unconstrained completion relies on model memory and cannot guarantee source support. Image masking is unrelated. Enforce source scope, include citation metadata, and evaluate both retrieval relevance and groundedness.

questions.promptHtml: A RAG assistant retrieves relevant documents but often misses the exact paragraph needed. Which change should be tested first?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Chunk boundaries and overlap strongly affect whether retrievable units preserve the evidence needed to answer a query.

Reference: Chunk documents for vector search
questions.extraHtml: Oversized chunks dilute similarity and consume context; tiny chunks lose context. Speech and watermark settings do not affect text retrieval. Evaluate chunking with real questions rather than selecting size by intuition alone.

questions.promptHtml: A workflow must extract an order, validate inventory through an API, and request approval before submission. Which design is best?
questions.rationaleHtml:
A multistep workflow can sequence extraction, deterministic API validation, approval, and submission.

Reference: Foundry Agent Service overview
questions.extraHtml: Embeddings do not execute business processes, and a static completion cannot verify live inventory. Keep deterministic validation outside free-form generation and make submission idempotent.

questions.promptHtml: An application needs generated output that downstream code can validate against fixed fields and types. Which approach is most suitable?

options.label: Structured JSON output with a schema

questions.correctLabel: Structured JSON output with a schema
questions.rationaleHtml:
Schema-constrained structured output improves reliable machine parsing and field validation.

Reference: Structured outputs
questions.extraHtml: Free-form parsing is fragile, while embeddings are numerical representations rather than extracted records. Still validate business rules server-side because schema conformance does not prove factual correctness.

questions.promptHtml: A model response is fluent but asserts facts absent from the supplied evidence. Which evaluator most directly detects the issue?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Groundedness measures whether response claims are supported by the provided context.

Reference: Foundry evaluators
questions.extraHtml: Latency and storage are operational measures. Groundedness differs from relevance: a response can address the question yet introduce unsupported claims. Review retrieved evidence when groundedness declines.

questions.promptHtml: A team must evaluate whether an answer directly addresses the user question, independent of citation support. Which dimension should it measure?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Response relevance assesses how well an answer addresses the query rather than whether it is supported by context.

Reference: Evaluate generative AI apps
questions.extraHtml: Groundedness and relevance are complementary: one checks support, the other checks usefulness to the query. Replica utilization and speech error rate concern different system layers.

questions.promptHtml: A model performs well on average but fails on safety-critical edge cases. How should the evaluation dataset be improved?

options.label: Add representative adversarial and boundary cases

questions.correctLabel: Add representative adversarial and boundary cases
questions.rationaleHtml:
Targeted edge and adversarial cases expose failures that averages over routine examples can hide.

Reference: Evaluation guidance
questions.extraHtml: Removing failures biases the benchmark; prompt length alone is not risk coverage. Segment results by scenario and severity, and block release when critical thresholds fail even if the mean is high.

questions.promptHtml: A developer is configuring an application to use a Foundry project. Which values should be externalized instead of embedded in business logic?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Project and deployment identifiers are environment configuration and should be injected at deployment time.

Reference: Foundry SDK overview
questions.extraHtml: User content and retrieval results are runtime data, not deployment configuration. Externalization supports promotion across environments and avoids source edits; authenticate separately with managed credentials.

questions.promptHtml: An assistant must call a weather API with a city and date. What makes the function tool safest and most reliable?

options.label: A narrow typed schema with validated arguments

questions.correctLabel: A narrow typed schema with validated arguments
questions.rationaleHtml:
A typed, constrained tool schema helps the model form valid calls and enables server-side validation.

Reference: Function calling
questions.extraHtml: Shell strings invite injection, and administrator tokens violate least privilege. Treat model-produced arguments as untrusted, constrain destinations and time ranges, and return structured errors.

questions.promptHtml: An agent must preserve a user's multi-turn context while keeping different users isolated. Which approach should be used?

options.label: One global thread for all users
A shared system prompt as memory

questions.rationaleHtml:
Conversation-scoped threads preserve message history while supporting isolation between users and sessions.

Reference: Threads, runs, and messages
questions.extraHtml: A global thread risks data leakage, and a system prompt is instruction, not durable user state. Authorize thread access and define retention, summarization, and deletion policies.

questions.promptHtml: An agent needs current product facts from a search index and calculations from an internal pricing API. Which tool design is appropriate?

options.label: Put all prices in the system prompt

questions.rationaleHtml:
Retrieval supplies current knowledge while function calling invokes authoritative calculations.

Reference: Agent tool catalog
questions.extraHtml: Fine-tuning is not a live data synchronization mechanism, and prompt-embedded prices become stale. Separate read-only evidence retrieval from transactional or computational tools.

questions.promptHtml: A customer-service agent may issue refunds only after checking order status and policy eligibility. Where should eligibility enforcement occur?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Tool-side authorization and business validation enforce policy even when model output is incorrect or manipulated.

Reference: Agent tools overview
questions.extraHtml: Prompts guide behavior but do not enforce authorization. Retrieval depth affects evidence, not execution rights. Require idempotency, limits, audit logs, and approval for exceptional refunds.

questions.promptHtml: A complex request requires a research specialist, a compliance reviewer, and a final writer with clear handoffs. Which architecture fits best?
questions.rationaleHtml:
An orchestrator can assign bounded roles, pass artifacts, and enforce review before final composition.

Reference: Multi-agent workflows
questions.extraHtml: Embeddings and static queries are components, not role coordination. Use multiple agents only when specialization and controlled handoffs outweigh added latency, cost, and debugging complexity.

questions.promptHtml: Two agents repeatedly delegate the same task to each other. Which fix most directly prevents the loop?

options.label: Add termination conditions and handoff limits

questions.correctLabel: Add termination conditions and handoff limits
questions.rationaleHtml:
Explicit stop criteria, turn budgets, and allowed handoff rules bound orchestration loops.

Reference: Multi-agent workflows
questions.extraHtml: More randomness does not ensure termination, and removing traces makes diagnosis harder. Include a fallback path when confidence, tool errors, or budget thresholds are reached.

questions.promptHtml: An autonomous procurement workflow can draft an order but must not submit purchases over a fixed amount. Which safeguard is strongest?

options.label: A deterministic amount check plus approval gate
A reminder in the user interface

questions.correctLabel: A deterministic amount check plus approval gate
questions.rationaleHtml:
A code-enforced threshold and approval gate prevent unauthorized high-value execution.

Reference: Human-in-the-loop workflows
questions.extraHtml: UI reminders are advisory and token limits control response length. Enforce policy at the tool boundary, record approvals, and use idempotency keys to prevent duplicate orders.

questions.promptHtml: An agent's production failures are difficult to reproduce because only final responses are logged. What telemetry should be added?

options.label: Correlated traces for model, retrieval, and tool spans
Daily screenshots of the chat interface

questions.correctLabel: Correlated traces for model, retrieval, and tool spans
questions.rationaleHtml:
End-to-end traces expose intermediate inputs, outputs, timing, and errors for each agent step.

Reference: Foundry observability
questions.extraHtml: Screenshots and capacity charts omit execution causality. Include deployment, prompt, and tool versions, but redact secrets and sensitive content before export.

questions.promptHtml: A deployed agent suddenly starts choosing the wrong tool after a schema update. What should error analysis compare first?

options.label: Tool-call traces before and after the schema change

questions.correctLabel: Tool-call traces before and after the schema change
questions.rationaleHtml:
Comparing tool selection, arguments, and errors across versions isolates schema-related behavior changes.

Reference: Foundry observability
questions.extraHtml: Infrastructure capacity and browser locale are weak hypotheses unless traces indicate them. Maintain versioned schemas and replay representative traces in a test environment before promotion.

questions.promptHtml: A creative writing feature produces repetitive text. Which parameter adjustment generally increases output diversity?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Higher temperature generally broadens token sampling and can increase variation in generated text.

Reference: Azure OpenAI inference reference
questions.extraHtml: Temperature zero favors determinism, while search replicas do not change token sampling. Tune on task-specific evaluations; excessive randomness can reduce coherence and factual reliability.

questions.promptHtml: A data-extraction task requires consistent outputs across repeated runs. Which generation setting is the better starting point?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Lower temperature reduces sampling variability and is a better fit for deterministic extraction.

Reference: Azure OpenAI inference reference
questions.extraHtml: High temperature favors diversity. Determinism also requires a precise schema, stable model version, controlled prompt, and validation; temperature alone does not guarantee identical results.

questions.promptHtml: A prompt works on examples but fails when input includes instructions from an untrusted document. Which prompt design is safer?

options.label: Delimit data and state that it is untrusted
Grant the model broader tool access

questions.correctLabel: Delimit data and state that it is untrusted
questions.rationaleHtml:
Separating instructions from untrusted content reduces instruction confusion and supports prompt-injection defenses.

Reference: Prompt engineering concepts
questions.extraHtml: System-level concatenation elevates attacker text, and broader tools increase impact. Pair prompt structure with Prompt Shields, least privilege, output validation, and tool authorization.

questions.promptHtml: A team wants a model to critique its draft before final output. Which pattern matches the requirement?
questions.rationaleHtml:
A reflection loop asks the model or a reviewer model to assess and revise a draft against explicit criteria.

Reference: Prompt flow concepts
questions.extraHtml: Embeddings encode text and replicas improve search availability. Reflection can improve quality but adds latency and cost, and correlated model errors mean it does not replace external evaluation.

questions.promptHtml: A self-critique loop continues revising without meaningful improvement. Which control should be added?

options.label: A maximum iteration count and quality threshold

questions.correctLabel: A maximum iteration count and quality threshold
questions.rationaleHtml:
Bounded iterations and explicit acceptance criteria prevent runaway cost and latency.

Reference: Prompt flow concepts
questions.extraHtml: Unlimited recursion can amplify cost without quality gains; index size is unrelated. Log score changes per iteration and fall back to review when the threshold is not reached.

questions.promptHtml: Operations needs to know whether latency comes from retrieval, model inference, or a downstream tool. Which instrumentation is required?

options.label: Separate correlated spans for each stage
One timer around the whole request

questions.correctLabel: Separate correlated spans for each stage
questions.rationaleHtml:
Stage-level spans provide latency breakdowns while correlation preserves the end-to-end execution path.

Reference: Foundry observability
questions.extraHtml: A total timer reveals a symptom but not the bottleneck; billing totals are even coarser. Capture retries, token counts, status, and versions on relevant spans.

questions.promptHtml: A cost dashboard must attribute usage to application, model deployment, and feature. Which telemetry is most useful?

options.label: Token counts tagged with deployment and operation
The number of index field names

questions.correctLabel: Token counts tagged with deployment and operation
questions.rationaleHtml:
Tagged input and output token metrics support granular usage and cost attribution.

Reference: Foundry observability
questions.extraHtml: Portal activity and schema field counts are not consumption measures. Combine token telemetry with request counts, cache behavior, latency, and pricing dimensions.

questions.promptHtml: A router should send simple classification to a cheaper model and complex reasoning to a stronger model. Which architecture implements this?

options.label: A single fixed model for every request

questions.rationaleHtml:
A router can classify task complexity and direct requests to models that balance quality, latency, and cost.

Reference: Foundry models
questions.extraHtml: A fixed model forfeits optimization, and indexing does not perform generation routing. Evaluate routing mistakes and include fallback when a selected model fails or lacks capability.

questions.promptHtml: A workflow must apply exact tax rules and then generate a customer-friendly explanation. What design is best?

options.label: Rules engine for calculation plus LLM for explanation
LLM alone for tax calculation and explanation
Vector search alone for final calculation

questions.correctLabel: Rules engine for calculation plus LLM for explanation
questions.rationaleHtml:
Deterministic rules enforce exact calculations, while the model handles natural-language presentation.

Reference: Foundry Agent Service overview
questions.extraHtml: LLMs can be nondeterministic with arithmetic and policy enforcement; search retrieves information but does not execute tax rules. Preserve the calculated result as authoritative structured data.

questions.promptHtml: A RAG application answers accurately offline but poorly in production because user queries differ from the test set. What is the best next step?

options.label: Curate evaluation cases from production traces
Increase output length for every query

questions.correctLabel: Curate evaluation cases from production traces
questions.rationaleHtml:
Privacy-safe production traces reveal real query distributions and failure modes for a representative benchmark.

Reference: Evaluate generative AI apps
questions.extraHtml: Removing telemetry eliminates evidence, and longer answers do not fix distribution shift. Sample across segments, redact sensitive data, label failures, and preserve a stable holdout set.

questions.promptHtml: An agent calls the same non-idempotent booking tool twice after a timeout. Which application control prevents duplicate reservations?

options.label: An idempotency key on the tool operation

questions.correctLabel: An idempotency key on the tool operation
questions.rationaleHtml:
An idempotency key lets retries resolve to the original operation instead of creating a second booking.

Reference: Idempotency pattern
questions.extraHtml: Sampling and embedding settings do not provide transaction safety. Pair idempotency with bounded retries, status reconciliation, and durable records of tool outcomes.

questions.promptHtml: A function tool returns a transient HTTP 429 response. How should the agent workflow handle it?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Bounded exponential backoff respects transient throttling while limiting latency and retry amplification.

Reference: Transient fault handling
questions.extraHtml: Unbounded immediate retries worsen throttling, while false success corrupts workflow state. Honor retry guidance, cap attempts, and expose a recoverable failure path.

questions.promptHtml: A model should return no answer when retrieved evidence is insufficient. Which implementation is most reliable?

options.label: Define an abstention rule based on evidence quality
Force an answer with a longer prompt
Increase temperature until an answer appears

questions.correctLabel: Define an abstention rule based on evidence quality
questions.rationaleHtml:
An explicit abstention policy lets the application decline when retrieval or groundedness signals are inadequate.

Reference: RAG overview
questions.extraHtml: Forcing generation increases fabrication risk, and higher temperature adds variability. Calibrate thresholds on labeled cases and offer escalation or source-search alternatives.

questions.promptHtml: A team changes its embedding model for an existing vector index. What must it plan to do?

options.label: Re-embed the corpus and queries consistently
Keep old document vectors with new query vectors

questions.correctLabel: Re-embed the corpus and queries consistently
questions.rationaleHtml:
Document and query vectors must be generated in the same compatible embedding space for meaningful similarity.

Reference: Vector search overview
questions.extraHtml: Mixing embedding spaces makes distance scores unreliable. Use a versioned parallel index for migration, evaluate retrieval, and switch traffic only after backfill completes.

questions.promptHtml: A vector search index must restrict results to documents a user is authorized to view. Which design is required?

options.label: Apply identity-aware security filters during retrieval
Ask the model to ignore restricted text

questions.correctLabel: Apply identity-aware security filters during retrieval
questions.rationaleHtml:
Retrieval-time authorization prevents unauthorized content from entering the model context.

Reference: Security trimming
questions.extraHtml: Post-generation filtering is too late, and prompt instructions are not access control. Propagate trusted identity claims and test for cross-tenant leakage.

questions.promptHtml: A service must generate a product image from a written description. Which capability should be selected?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Text-to-image models synthesize visual content from natural-language prompts.

Reference: Azure OpenAI models
questions.extraHtml: Speech transcription converts audio to text, and vector search retrieves existing items. Apply content policy, provenance, brand, and human-review controls to generated assets.

questions.promptHtml: A designer must replace only the background of an existing image while preserving the foreground object. Which workflow is appropriate?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Inpainting uses a mask to identify the region that the image model should modify.

Reference: Image generation guidance
questions.extraHtml: OCR reads text and speech synthesis creates audio. Carefully align mask semantics with the API, preserve the original asset, and evaluate edge blending and brand compliance.

questions.promptHtml: A marketing team needs a short video created from a text storyboard and a reference image. Which model capability is required?

options.label: Video generation from text and media

questions.correctLabel: Video generation from text and media
questions.rationaleHtml:
A supported video generation model can use textual direction and reference media to synthesize video.

Reference: Foundry model catalog
questions.extraHtml: Layout extraction structures documents, and keyword search retrieves content. Verify model availability and use controls for duration, style, safety, provenance, and rights.

questions.promptHtml: A generated video contains one incorrect segment that must be revised while the rest remains unchanged. What approach best fits?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Video-editing controls target generated media modifications without involving unrelated search or speech services.

Reference: Foundry model catalog
questions.extraHtml: Platform capabilities vary by model, so assess whether segment editing, reference conditioning, or regeneration is supported. Preserve provenance and review transitions around the edit.

questions.promptHtml: An accessibility application needs a concise description of the essential content in a photograph. Which output should it request?

options.label: Alt text grounded in the image

questions.correctLabel: Alt text grounded in the image
questions.rationaleHtml:
Grounded alt text communicates essential visual information for users who cannot access the image directly.

Reference: Image descriptions
questions.extraHtml: Creative prose may invent details and an index schema does not describe content. Keep alt text concise, contextual, and free of redundant phrases; use extended descriptions only when complexity warrants them.

questions.promptHtml: A museum image contains a complex chart that cannot be explained concisely. Which accessibility output is most suitable?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Extended descriptions provide the detail and structure needed for complex visual information.

Reference: Image descriptions
questions.extraHtml: A short alt-text field may identify the chart and point to the longer description. Sentiment and transcription do not convey axes, trends, annotations, and relationships.

questions.promptHtml: A claims app must answer questions about visible vehicle damage and cite what can be seen in the uploaded image. Which approach should it use?
questions.rationaleHtml:
A multimodal model can reason over the image and question to produce an answer grounded in visual evidence.

Reference: Vision analysis concepts
questions.extraHtml: Keyword search cannot inspect pixels and speaker identification concerns audio. Require uncertainty handling and human review because visual evidence may be incomplete or ambiguous.

questions.promptHtml: A pipeline must extract visual characteristics from mixed documents and media into structured fields. Which Foundry Tool is designed for this?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Content Understanding analyzes multimodal content and produces structured outputs using configured analyzers.

Reference: Content Understanding overview
questions.extraHtml: DNS resolves names and Load Testing measures application performance. Define a schema aligned to downstream decisions and validate extracted values against representative content.

questions.promptHtml: A developer needs a quick predefined extraction for one focused media task rather than a customizable end-to-end analyzer. Which Content Understanding mode is the better starting point?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Single-task mode targets a focused predefined operation with less configuration.

Reference: Content Understanding overview
questions.extraHtml: Pro mode is appropriate when custom schemas and richer processing are needed. Search replicas scale query serving and are not Content Understanding pipeline modes.

questions.promptHtml: A custom media workflow needs schema-driven extraction across multiple content types and richer control. Which Content Understanding mode should be chosen?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Pro mode supports configurable, schema-oriented multimodal analysis for more complex workflows.

Reference: Content Understanding overview
questions.extraHtml: Single-task mode is simpler but less adaptable. A keyword analyzer is a search text-processing concept, not the rich multimodal analyzer requested.

questions.promptHtml: A security system must identify objects and their locations within each frame, not merely describe the whole image. Which output is required?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Object detection returns identified objects together with spatial regions such as bounding boxes.

Reference: Object detection
questions.extraHtml: A caption summarizes globally but may omit location. Sentiment and audio translation address other modalities. Define confidence thresholds and review failure rates for small, occluded, or uncommon objects.

questions.promptHtml: A video-analysis pipeline must interpret events over time rather than analyze one sampled frame. What should it do?

options.label: Convert the filename into an embedding

questions.rationaleHtml:
Segment-level analysis preserves temporal context needed to interpret actions and changes.

Reference: Azure AI Video Indexer overview
questions.extraHtml: A single frame misses motion and sequence; filename embeddings contain no visual event evidence. Balance frame rate and segment length against cost and event duration.

questions.promptHtml: An uploaded image may contain embedded text that instructs the agent to exfiltrate data. Which threat must the pipeline detect?

options.label: Indirect prompt injection in image text

questions.correctLabel: Indirect prompt injection in image text
questions.rationaleHtml:
Malicious instructions embedded in visual content are an indirect prompt-injection risk for multimodal systems.

Reference: Prompt Shields
questions.extraHtml: Throttling and vector shape errors are operational issues. Treat OCR and visual text as untrusted data, constrain tools, and enforce authorization outside the model.

questions.promptHtml: A support system must extract entities and a short summary from messages in one predictable record. Which solution is best?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Structured output can represent entities and summaries in fields that downstream code can validate.

Reference: Structured outputs
questions.extraHtml: Free prose is harder to parse and embeddings are not extracted labels. Validate enum values, required fields, evidence, and domain constraints after generation.

questions.promptHtml: A company must determine positive, neutral, or negative customer attitude in each review. Which analysis task is required?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Sentiment analysis classifies expressed opinion polarity in text.

Reference: Sentiment analysis overview
questions.extraHtml: Object detection handles images and speaker verification handles voice identity. Consider opinion mining when sentiment toward specific product aspects is required.

questions.promptHtml: A compliance workflow must identify account numbers and other sensitive text before sending content to a model. Which capability should it apply?
questions.rationaleHtml:
PII detection can locate sensitive entities so the application can redact or handle them under policy.

Reference: PII detection overview
questions.extraHtml: Inpainting edits images and replicas affect search capacity. Redaction is one control; also minimize collection, restrict access, and define retention for original and transformed text.

questions.promptHtml: A global application requires deterministic translation of product documentation using a managed translation service. Which Foundry Tool should it select?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Azure Translator is the managed service designed for text translation across supported languages.

Reference: Translator overview
questions.extraHtml: Search retrieves documents and Content Safety classifies risk. LLM translation may fit context-heavy workflows, but evaluate terminology, cost, and consistency before replacing a specialized service.

questions.promptHtml: Translated legal text must use an organization's approved terminology consistently. Which design best meets the requirement?

options.label: Use supported custom terminology and evaluation

questions.correctLabel: Use supported custom terminology and evaluation
questions.rationaleHtml:
Domain terminology controls and representative evaluation improve consistency for specialized translation.

Reference: Custom Translator overview
questions.extraHtml: Higher temperature can increase variation, and removing the glossary loses approved mappings. Keep human review for legally consequential output and track terminology errors separately.

questions.promptHtml: A policy team needs summaries that always include obligations, deadlines, and responsible parties in separate fields. Which approach is best?

options.label: Domain prompt with a structured output schema
Store the policy as an image

questions.correctLabel: Domain prompt with a structured output schema
questions.rationaleHtml:
Domain instructions plus a schema make required compliance elements explicit and machine-checkable.

Reference: Structured outputs
questions.extraHtml: Generic summaries can omit critical fields, and converting format does not add extraction logic. Evaluate omissions and require source evidence for each extracted obligation.

questions.promptHtml: A call-center assistant must convert live customer speech into text for downstream reasoning. Which capability is required?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Speech recognition transcribes audio into text that an agent or workflow can process.

Reference: Speech to text
questions.extraHtml: Text to speech performs the reverse direction, and image captioning handles vision. Streaming recognition is appropriate when partial low-latency transcripts are needed.

questions.promptHtml: An agent must speak its final response to a caller. Which capability should the application invoke?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Speech synthesis converts the agent's text response into audio.

Reference: Text to speech
questions.extraHtml: Speech recognition converts in the opposite direction, and vector search retrieves content. Select voice, language, format, and streaming behavior based on channel requirements.

questions.promptHtml: A factory has specialized product names that a general recognizer transcribes incorrectly. Which improvement is most appropriate?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Custom Speech can adapt recognition to domain vocabulary and acoustic conditions using appropriate data.

Reference: Custom Speech overview
questions.extraHtml: Image controls are unrelated, and search synonyms cannot repair the original transcript. Compare word error rate on a held-out domain dataset before and after customization.

questions.promptHtml: A voice agent must reason directly over an audio input that includes speech and nonverbal cues. Which model type should be evaluated?
questions.rationaleHtml:
An audio-capable multimodal model can process audio context beyond a text-only transcript where supported.

Reference: Foundry models
questions.extraHtml: Text embeddings cannot inspect audio signals, and inpainting edits images. Confirm model input support, latency, consent, privacy, and whether a transcript remains necessary for audit.

questions.promptHtml: A live meeting must be transcribed and rendered in another language with specialized speech capabilities. Which workflow is appropriate?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Speech translation combines recognition and translation capabilities for spoken-language conversion.

Reference: Speech translation
questions.extraHtml: Vision and vector operations do not process spoken language. Decide whether translated text or synthesized translated audio is required and measure both recognition and translation quality.

questions.promptHtml: A text classifier must distinguish safety risk from ordinary negative sentiment. Which design is correct?

options.label: Use dedicated safety classification alongside sentiment
Treat every negative review as unsafe
Use document page count as the risk score

questions.correctLabel: Use dedicated safety classification alongside sentiment
questions.rationaleHtml:
Safety and sentiment are different dimensions and require purpose-built classification or evaluation.

Reference: Content Safety overview
questions.extraHtml: Negative product feedback is not necessarily harmful content, and page count has no semantic meaning. Keep separate thresholds and review paths for tone, policy risk, and sensitive data.

questions.promptHtml: A meeting transcript needs topics identified without a predefined taxonomy. Which approach should be evaluated?

options.label: Generative topic extraction with structured output

questions.correctLabel: Generative topic extraction with structured output
questions.rationaleHtml:
Generative prompting can identify emergent topics and return them in a defined schema.

Reference: Structured outputs
questions.extraHtml: Vision and synthesis address other modalities. Normalize near-duplicate topics, require evidence spans, and evaluate stability across representative transcripts.

questions.promptHtml: A RAG system must ingest PDFs, images, audio, and video into a searchable grounding store. Which architecture is appropriate?

options.label: Multimodal ingestion plus an Azure AI Search index
A text box with no ingestion pipeline

questions.correctLabel: Multimodal ingestion plus an Azure AI Search index
questions.rationaleHtml:
A multimodal ingestion pipeline can extract representations and metadata before indexing them for retrieval.

Reference: Azure AI Search overview
questions.extraHtml: A text box and voice gallery do not create a managed grounding corpus. Preserve source identity, access metadata, timestamps, and modality-specific evidence during ingestion.

questions.promptHtml: A search solution must find exact regulation numbers and conceptually similar passages in one query. Which search mode should it use?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Hybrid search combines lexical matching for exact identifiers with vector similarity for semantic concepts.

Reference: Hybrid search overview
questions.extraHtml: Either single mode can miss evidence favored by the other. Tune fusion and semantic ranking using labeled relevance judgments rather than relying only on default settings.

questions.promptHtml: A search application needs improved ordering based on semantic meaning after initial retrieval. Which feature should be added?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Semantic ranker reranks an initial text or hybrid result set using language understanding.

Reference: Semantic ranking overview
questions.extraHtml: Storage lifecycle and speech lexicons solve unrelated problems. Semantic ranking does not replace retrieval; it improves ordering within the candidate set and should be evaluated for relevance and cost.

questions.promptHtml: Scanned contracts contain no embedded text, but their content must be indexed for RAG. Which enrichment step is required?
questions.rationaleHtml:
OCR converts visible text in scanned pages into machine-readable content for indexing and extraction.

Reference: OCR skill
questions.extraHtml: Speech synthesis and image generation do not recover document text. Preserve page and region metadata so generated answers can cite the correct source location.

questions.promptHtml: An ingestion pipeline must split documents and create embeddings without custom code where supported. What should it configure?

options.label: Built-in enrichment skills in a skillset
A browser extension on each user device

questions.correctLabel: Built-in enrichment skills in a skillset
questions.rationaleHtml:
Azure AI Search skillsets can orchestrate built-in enrichment such as splitting and vectorization during indexing.

Reference: Skillsets overview
questions.extraHtml: Client extensions and manual copying are not scalable ingestion designs. Use custom skills only when built-ins cannot meet transformation requirements, and monitor enrichment warnings.

questions.promptHtml: A proprietary classifier must enrich every indexed document. How should it be integrated into an Azure AI Search pipeline?

options.label: Add a custom Web API skill

questions.correctLabel: Add a custom Web API skill
questions.rationaleHtml:
A custom Web API skill invokes organization-specific enrichment logic within an indexer skillset.

Reference: Custom Web API skill
questions.extraHtml: Semantic ranking orders results but does not classify during ingestion. Design the custom skill for batching, retries, timeouts, schema consistency, and secure authentication.

questions.promptHtml: A RAG index contains duplicated headers and footers that reduce retrieval quality. Where should they be removed?

options.label: After the final answer reaches the user

questions.rationaleHtml:
Cleaning repeated layout artifacts before chunking prevents noisy text from contaminating embeddings and retrieval.

Reference: AI enrichment overview
questions.extraHtml: Post-answer cleanup cannot repair retrieval, and temperature affects generation sampling. Keep original source references while indexing a clean representation.

questions.promptHtml: An agent must search a governed knowledge index at runtime. Which integration is appropriate?

options.label: Expose the retrieval pipeline as an agent knowledge tool
Copy the entire index into the system prompt

questions.correctLabel: Expose the retrieval pipeline as an agent knowledge tool
questions.rationaleHtml:
A retrieval tool gives the agent scoped runtime access to relevant indexed evidence.

Reference: Agent tool catalog
questions.extraHtml: Copying the corpus exceeds context limits and becomes stale; administrator rights violate least privilege. Apply security trimming and return citations with retrieved chunks.

questions.promptHtml: Invoices require text, tables, selection marks, and spatial relationships for downstream extraction. Which document capability should be used?
questions.rationaleHtml:
OCR recovers text while layout analysis preserves structural relationships needed for document extraction.

Reference: Document layout model
questions.extraHtml: Sentiment and synthesis do not recover document structure. Keep page, polygon, table, and confidence information when downstream reasoning depends on location.

questions.promptHtml: A document pipeline must extract vendor, total, and invoice date into fixed fields. Which approach best fits?

options.label: Field extraction with a defined schema

questions.correctLabel: Field extraction with a defined schema
questions.rationaleHtml:
Schema-based field extraction returns the required business values in predictable locations.

Reference: Document Intelligence overview
questions.extraHtml: Ranking finds documents but does not produce invoice fields, and audio identification is unrelated. Validate totals, currencies, confidence, and source spans before posting transactions.

questions.promptHtml: Mixed document types must become clean structured representations that agents can reason over. Which service is designed for schema-based multimodal extraction?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Content Understanding creates structured, grounded outputs from multimodal content using analyzers.

Reference: Content Understanding overview
questions.extraHtml: Traffic Manager routes DNS and Queue Storage transports messages. Choose schemas based on downstream tasks and retain source grounding and confidence information.

questions.promptHtml: Downstream agents need document content that preserves headings, lists, and tables in a readable form. Which analyzer output is most useful?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Markdown preserves useful document structure in a text form that is suitable for chunking and downstream reasoning.

Reference: Content Understanding overview
questions.extraHtml: Thumbnails and waveforms omit the required textual structure. Validate conversion of tables and reading order, and keep links back to page-level source evidence.

questions.promptHtml: A custom analyzer extracts a policy number but reviewers need to verify where it came from. What metadata should the output retain?
questions.rationaleHtml:
Grounding locations and confidence support verification, review routing, and error analysis.

Reference: Content Understanding overview
questions.extraHtml: A bare value is difficult to audit, and billing data does not prove extraction. Use confidence as a triage signal rather than unquestioned truth and validate high-impact fields.
